user: How can I resolve performance issues related to the portmap plug-in in Calico CNI on IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service when iptables rules are not updating or the calico-node container restarts unexpectedly?
assistant: Sorry, but I do not have that information.
user: How can I update the Calico installation?
assistant: To update the Calico installation on IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service, follow these steps:
1. Use the command `oc edit installation default -n calico-system` to edit the default Calico installation resource.
2. In the `spec.calicoNetwork` section, change the value of the `mtu` field to your desired value.
3. Save and close the file.
4. Apply the MTU changes by rebooting all worker nodes in your cluster.
Please note that the MTU should be equal to or greater than 1450 bytes to ensure the proper functioning of your Red Hat OpenShift cluster.
user: What does the portmap plug-in do?
assistant: The portmap plug-in for the Calico Container Network Interface (CNI) allows you to use hostPorts to expose your application pods on specific ports of the worker nodes. However, when there are numerous services within the cluster or many ports used by those services, the portmap plug-in can create an excessive number of iptables rules, which may lead to performance issues. 
If the calico-node container restarts unexpectedly or if the iptables rules fail to update, you might consider disabling the portmap plug-in by removing it from your cluster's Calico CNI configuration. However, if you need to use hostPorts, it is not recommended to disable the portmap plug-in.The portmap plug-in for the Calico container network interface (CNI) allows you to use a hostPort to expose your application pods on a specific port on the worker node. user: Is it possible to Increase or decrease the Calico plug-in maximum transmission unit (MTU)?
assistant: yes, you can adjust the maximum transmission unit (MTU) of the Calico plug-in by modifying the default Calico installation resource. In the `spec.calicoNetwork` section, change the value of the `mtu` field to your desired setting. After making your changes, save and close the file. To apply the MTU changes, reboot all worker nodes in your cluster. Please note that the MTU should be set to 1450 bytes or greater to ensure the proper functioning of your Red Hat OpenShift cluster.
user: How can I check the current setting?
assistant: To check the current MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit) setting for the Calico plug-in, examine the `mtu` field in the `spec.calicoNetwork` section of the default Calico installation resource. You can view this resource by running the command `oc edit installation default -n calico-system` in your terminal. The current MTU value will be displayed next to the `mtu` label.
user: Is that the only way to do it?

user: Jumbo Frames
assistant: Jumbo Frames are Ethernet frames with a payload more significant than the standard maximum transmission unit (MTU) of 1,500 bytes. They are used on local area networks that support at least 1 Gbps and can be as large as 9,000 bytes. Jumbo Frames need to be configured the same on the entire network path from the source device to the destination device. If the whole chain isn't set the same, it defaults to the lowest setting along the chain. IBM Cloud currently has network devices set to 9,000. All customer devices need to be set to the same 9,000 value for best performance.

[The End of Previous Conversation]

[The Start of Current Turn Question]
How is it configure?
[The End of Current Turn Question]

[The Start of Reference Answer]
To configure Jumbo Frames, you need to edit the network configuration file for the eth0 interface on your system. For CentOS, RHEL, and Fedora users, you would edit the /etc/sysconfig/network-scripts/ifcfg-eth0 file, while Debian and Ubuntu users would edit the /etc/network/interfaces file. Once you have made the necessary changes to the file, you can close and save it, then restart the Interface eth0. This action will cause a brief loss of network connectivity. You can configure jumbo frames for the following operating systems.
Linux: Debian, Ubuntu, CentOS, Red Hat Enterprise Linux
Windows
Here are the specific steps for each operating system:
CentOS, RHEL, Fedora:
1. Open the network configuration file for the eth0 interface using the vi editor:
  vi /etc/sysconfig/network-scripts/ifcfg-eth0
2. Add the following configuration directive to specify the size of the frame in bytes:
  MTU 9000
3. Save and close the file.
4. Restart the Interface eth0:
  /etc/init.d/networking restart
Debian and Ubuntu:
1. Open the network configuration file for the eth0 interface using the vi editor:
  vi /etc/network/interfaces
2. Add the following configuration directive to specify the size of the frame in bytes:
  MTU=9000
3. Save and close the file.
4. Restart the Interface eth0:
  /etc/init.d/networking restart
Please note that for best performance, all devices on the network path from the source device to the destination device need to be configured with the same MTU value. IBM Cloud has network devices set to 9,000, so for best performance, all customer devices should be set to the same 9,000 value.
[The End of Reference Answer]
